svg.title: Archon 1.0: talk to one orchestrator, command a fleet of agents
svg.desc: Chat, archon say, watched GitHub mentions and recurring Aether requests reach one orchestrator. A persistent backlog feeds eighteen built-in default pipelines or your own pipelines, defined in TOML with stage prompts, for all repositories or just one. The daemon enforces caps, budgets, model policy and an autonomy ceiling; merging is manual by default. Six illustrated default pipelines show stages, fan-out and bounded failure loops. Ship modes are pr and local. Lavish is optional: use its pages or the CLI for reports, proposals and questions. Archon runs on Aether.

svg.text: A hierarchical orchestration layer on Aether.
Tell one orchestrator what you want. It plans,
queues and delegates across all your repos.
Also: @archon on watched GitHub repos · recurring Aether schedules

g.text: fix api login; update web with strict review
web · chose strict-pr-review for this change

svg.text: ONE LONG-LIVED AETHER AGENT · SUPERVISED BY ARCHOND

g.text: Priorities, dependencies, retries. Saved in SQLite.
The orchestrator decides. The daemon enforces.
Caps per fleet, repository and pipeline
Budgets per item, per day and lifetime
Model policy: allow, deny, maximum effort
Manual merge by default · pause / resume

svg.text: It picks the pipeline, the model and the effort.

g.text: One reviewer and a fix loop.
Agents use it like a real user.

svg.text: or write your own: TOML + stage prompts
stages can fan out to several agents

g.text: A worker fleet, across every repo.
worktrees · team roles get their own

svg.text: The orchestrator and stage workers run as Aether agents using native engine CLIs.
Say it once. Archon runs the fleet.
HIERARCHICAL | PERSISTENT | QUIET BY DEFAULT | BUILT ON AETHER
